en:
Logus was anxious to get back out to the water once he knew it would be safe, but he seemed reluctant to just abandon you to the island. Seeing an opportunity for a compromise, you appointed him Admiral of Lukatt's navy.

He tearfully and graciously accepted the offer, and worked hard to oversee the rebuilding of just such a navy.

He spends more time in port than at sea, but he makes a point of captaining each new ship's maiden voyage and reporting to you in person on just how well the efforts are going.

Admiral Logus remains a wise, available advisor, and a good friend.

en:
As your conquest of the island became inevitable, Grant returned to Hayill, and eventually became your point of contact with the Lycanthropes who made their home there.

You still see him on occasion, mostly when it is time to discuss relations or policy, and he acts the same as he ever did, approaching his duty with a hard-swallowed stoicism.

Hayill eventually becomes an important source of manpower, as the indefatigable people there spread out across the island, and werewolves become a common sight in the fledgling communities.

en:
With the blessing of his father, Grant remained with you, to serve as a symbol of the Lycanthropes dedication to the new nation.

He has remained close, helpful, and eager to pitch in, whether you need an extra pair of hands with rebuilding or an extra pair of folded arms at a negotiation table.

Owing to his high visibility, Hayill soon sees a fair amount of immigration from the mainland and becomes a secondary hub for your government, overseeing the entirety of the Knightwood region.

Werewolf guardsmen in uniform are a common sight in western towns, and common folk, once wary, have come to rely upon them.

Grant is very proud of this, and remains your confidant and friend.

en:
Greave took the reformation of the island very seriously, and ended up making it his personal mission to dismantle the stocks and other facilities like it.

He met surprisingly little opposition, and eventually gathered what few good guardsmen he could find and returned to the Crest mainland to make sure that the general populace heard all about what Lukatt really was.

His news enraged the people, most of whom had a friend of a friend who had been shipped out, and now, at the risk of making enemies of a lot of powerful men, he is trying to start an inquest to uncover corruption within Crest's judiciary system.

en:
Greave swore that he wouldn't let another travesty like the stocks occur again, so when the island was taken, he asked you to put him in charge of dismantling the remaining facilities.

When he and his team marched on the stocks, they found them severely undermanned, and quickly rounded up what soldiers and prisoners remained.

With a little work, he was able to convert the stocks into a coastal stronghold, and he remains there, helping to coordinate rebuilding efforts on the west coast of the island.

Mainly, he focuses on preventing Crest infiltrators from interfering with the development of the young nation, and he remains dedicated and driven.

en:
Once a permanent stronghold was established, Greening appointed himself "dinnermaster" and set up a community eatery.

He relies on some good old-fashioned cooking for the most part, only very occasionally (he promises) testing out his magicks on unsuspecting diners.

For the most part, he remains well-liked among the people, and is glad to be using his talents for roasting entrees instead of enemies.

en:
Greening seemed a bit lost once rebuilding efforts began, and was not particularly well-suited to the requisite labour.

He made an effort to help out with provisioning whenever he could, and seemed to really enjoy it, so once you had enough hands to keep things running without him, you suggested that he open his own cafe, and he took to the notion with enthusiastic delight.

He fussed over the precise design and layout of the place for far longer than was necessary, but eventually, he opened shop, and now he and a few carefully-trained assistants run a tight business.

His cafe is particularly popular with visiting dignitaries who appreciate his eccentric taste and attention to detail, and he seems happy to be there.

en:
Kirilo took almost immediately to watching out for newly-arriving immigrants, accompanying convoys along the roads and making sure that everybody was safely settled in.

You hear mixed reports regarding him, some appreciative and others less so, but he is trying his best to stay involved and to give honest people a chance to dig in to their new lives.

en:
Kirilo seemed like he was going to involve himself regardless, so when smaller communities of immigrants began to form on the island, you appointed Kirilo the head of security for a group of them and gave him the authority and funds to hire his own people.

He makes regular reports to you as to the status of his districts, and all reports suggest that under his guidance, those communities have remained very safe. 

He remains well-regarded by the downtrodden (and formerly downtrodden), and would have it no other way.

en:
Leftie's mood turned foul as more people arrived on the island, and after the first few loads of immigrants arrived, he withdrew.

You heard rumors that a man matching his description was spotted with a ragtag mercenary crew.

Though you can't be certain if those rumors are true or not, one thing you can be sure of is that Leftie wants no part of civilized life.

en:
When you chose to keep Leftie close instead of cutting him free, something moved within the giant man, and he devoted himself to you and to your campaigns wholeheartedly.

His breadth of experience working odd jobs and his unsinkable constitution have made him an invaluable asset to the rebuilding efforts, and he is high in demand when labour teams are being chosen.

Being away from the mainland long-term seems to have given him some sense of closure, and he works hard to ensure that his second chance at life is not wasted.

He makes his home near your capital stronghold, and still makes efforts to see you as often as he can. He often tells you to call upon him at the slightest need, and regards you highly as both a leader and as a friend.

en:
Although Moria participated eagerly in the conquest of the island, once all of the major battles had been won, she had little interest in participating further.

She left to live on her own, away from the conveniences and confines of civilization, and you have heard no reports of her at all.

Presumably she is happier to be left alone.

en:
Moria, having been disillusioned on the trappings of modern civilization already, seemed uneasy when your campaigns shifted from battle to rebuilding. She clearly didn't want to be part of the bustle of new and growing communities.

Knowing that she preferred her life to be hard-fought, you asked her if she would consider helping on the frontiers as a ranger, hunting and scouting, and this idea seemed to appeal to her.

You hardly ever hear from her anymore, but she is spotted from time to time in town, selling pelts or meat at the marketplaces, and sometimes guiding lost travelers to safe communities.

She clearly prefers to be left alone, but her continued participation tells you that she is content.

en:
Nazar made good on his promise to keep your shoulders warm, and he has cheerfully made a space for himself in your bed every night since that night in the old church.

Once events with Crest began to settle down, and it became clear that life on the island would be more relaxed, the two of you were married formally, in a grand ceremony in the capital, before a crowd of hundreds of cheering Lukattites.

Supporting both your efforts to help reconstruct life on the island and you personally, people began to quietly compare him to the memory of Maxim Spartill, lord consort of the island's last queen.

As the closest and dearest admirer of his heroic form and demeanor, you find that comparison difficult to argue.

en:
Nazar was seemingly involved in everything once events on the island began to pick up. 

He participated eagerly in both the conquest and the rebuilding effort, lending a cheerful hand to anyone who asked.

He still comes by your stronghold to see you from time to time, and last you heard from him, he was working with a shipbiulding crew in Greenback Bay.

en:
Nazar was eager to involve himself with the labour crews once rebuilding began, and quickly established himself as "foreman" once again.

He remained close to you, even as rebuilding efforts spread across the island, and you began to hear rumors that he was gaining something of a reputation as a heartbreaker. Apparently he attracted a great number of interested suitors, yet rebuffed them all.

When you asked him about it in friendly conversation, he seemed rather embarassed, telling you that there was in fact someone whose eye he was hoping to catch.

Nazar remains close by, making himself available for whatever you need, and continuing to turn away suitors while waiting patiently for the one he really wants to notice him.

en:
Paul seemed a bit lost after the island was conquered, unsure whether to celebrate with everyone else or not.

Though most people seemed to have no problem with him or with giants in general, he seemed self-conscious. He went back to being a labourer for hire, ensuring that only those who truly wanted his services would have them.

Most recent reports say that he is employed with a logging crew in the Knightwood region, where his knowledge of the terrain and great strength are high in demand.

en:
Once the conquest of the island was complete, Paul quickly became instrumental in the rebuilding efforts.

He and some of the others came together and formed their own organization to coordinate divisions of labour and supplies, and Paul was there in the thick of it. He was frequently seen inspecting shipments in port and reviewing building sites to ensure that the work was solid.

He has since established a headquarters for his guild in Greenback Bay, where he hosts visiting experts and workers as needed.

Although you did not personally oversee its formation, Paul makes a point of reporting the labour guild's progress to you, perhaps more as an excuse to see you face-to-face than out of necessity, and he remains very loudly fond of you.

en:
Peregrine particularly delighted in the conquest of the island and the struggle with Crest that followed immediately thereafter.

He traveled back and forth between Lukatt and the mainland regularly, being something of a deliberate thorn in the side of haughty politicians, and using the island as a sort of safe home base.

You have, of course, heard rumors of this, but no official complaints or reports have come to you, so for the time being, it seems unnecessary to interfere.

en:
With a lack of anyone wealthy to plunder, or indeed, a lack of much use for wealth on the island at all, Peregrine found himself living his cover story full time once the island's conquest was secured.

He moved to Greenback Bay and helped out at first with the crews building Lukatt's new navy, and then later hiring on to shipping voyages.

He clearly prefers life on the move, and is so hard to track that you rarely see him, but every once in a great while, he'll stop in and force you to make time to share a drink or a dirty story.

en:
Rangda eagerly lent her sword to the conquest of the island, and was one of the first to pledge herself as a permanent citizen of Lukatt.

She was instrumental in the formation of Lukatt's military, eager to work with veterans and soldiers outside of the context of Tsarath's laws, and she even spearheaded a training program specifically for women and girls.

Reports on her progress suggest that she is not particularly popular with her recruits, however, as she tends to be harder on them than even the standard military training programs.

Attendance in her program is low, and the dropout rate is high.

en:
Rangda was adamant that she be involved with the reformation of Lukatt's military forces, and so once the conquest was complete, she set up a training camp for willing recruits.

Though her teaching style was at first harsh and unpopular, she regularly came to you for advice, and eventually, she relaxed a little and learned to meet the students halfway. Attendance in her program is soaring, with a steady stream of fresh-faced men and women willing and ready to pitch in and defend their new homeland.

She is now an officer in the growing ranks of Lukatt's military, and she seems pleased to have found a place where she can live the life she chooses.

en:
Rosaline was happy to be a part of the young nation rising on Lukatt, and offered her services to you as an informant and a spy.

Though you had some doubts initially, a few test cases have proven her extraordinarily competent in this regard, and she was able to give you ample warning in a few situations when agitators from Crest planned to undermine your new nation.

She is a constant fixture in your stronghold and at any political arrangements that arise, and she seems pleased to be involved.

en:
When politics began creeping in to the island, Rosaline insisted on offering her services to you as an informant and spy. Seeing that she would not be dissuaded, you accepted her offer.

Ostensibly, she haunts your events as a courtesan, sometimes as a Lukattite and other times masquerading as a foreign dignitary. Her extensive training in subterfuge serve her well in this, often providing interesting insight, and she soon becomes indispensable at the negotiating table.

She insists that she finds the intrigue of court both more palatable than assassinations and more fun than she had expected, so she remains on hand, eager to attend any event you need her for.

en:
When the conquest was complete, Shapiro did what any self-respecting sorcerer would do; he hired a crew to build an ominous tower a short distance from your stronghold and moved in.

He spends his days in isolation, researching and experimenting, venturing out only once in a while to browse the markets for supplies or to replace a singed coat, and he seems quite content to play the role of the hermit wizard.

en:
Once your permanent stronghold was secured, Shapiro set out to establish a formal guild of magic on the island, a task he claimed was more borne of necessity than of desire. With a little time and effort, he was eventually able to arrange an appropriate facility a short distance away from your capital.

Though his demeanor is at a times cold and unsettling, his knowledge regarding magic is undeniably broad, and his experience in guild practice and politics has been especially valuable as your people continue to uncover strange arcana all over the island.

He makes himself available for consultation whenever any relevant situations arise, but mostly he happily keeps to himself in the new guild, taking apprentices, conducting his (assuredly safe) experiments, and giving the arcane arts a solid foothold in your new home.

en:
Vankan stayed with you during and after the conquest of the island, seemingly reluctant to let you out of his sight.

Though he said nothing and put on a cheerful face, something was clearly bothering him.

One day, as negotiations with Crest dignitaries were about to commence, one of the man's aides pulled a blow gun and launched a dart at you. As if he knew it was coming, Vankan threw himself in front of you, and the dart struck him instead.

He died in your arms a moment later, ravaged by poison as your guards put your would-be assassin to the sword, but when he went, his face seemed peaceful.

en:
Relieved beyond measure that you had not been forced to slay Leviathan, Vankan devoted himself to the divine beast's worship. His unique gift apparently made it easier for him to commune, and so Vankan alternately serves you as an advisor and, when it is needed, as a mouthpiece for Leviathan.

Despite his protests, a small cult has risen up around him, and you have encouraged him to accept the role and to guide them with compassion and humility.

His newfound "Sunken Order" works tirelessly to help new settlers however they can, and to remind people to thank Leviathan for their small fortunes, and Leviathan tells you, both through Vankan's voice and through his brief communions with you, that he is pleased at their efforts.

As for Vankan himself, he is busier than ever before, but also seems at peace, and still regards you most warmly.

en:
Wisaka stayed with you during the conquest of the island, but afterward, when the adventuring gave way to rebuilding and politics, he lost interest.

He left your company and made way for Hayill in order to be with other lycanthropes, but even that place failed to hold his interest for long.

Now, you hear people talk from time to time of "The Howling Bard" who wanders from place to place, meeting new people every day but never content to stay around for long.

en:
Wisaka seemed to have no place to fit in once the rebuilding started, but for his fondness of you personally, he stuck around anyway. He talked about going to Hayill from time to time, but never actually packed up and left.

Once you began receiving foreign dignitaries in your stronghold, however, things began to change. Idly plucking away at his lute one day in court, a visiting noblewoman became absolutely enraptured with him. She immediately contracted the construction of a summer home on the island, and she positively insists on organizing eccentric annual festivals that showcase the varied talents of native Lukattites.

Opinions of these festivals range from inspired to tasteless, but Wisaka features prominently, and he seems thrilled to be widely known and well-regarded.

en:
Zantanak remained by your side faithfully and obediently, serving as your bodyguard and advisor continually, as your pact with him demanded.

Loathe to wear a disguise, he has taken to dressing in regal fineries and making a show of his advisory role, and he seems to take great pleasure in the startled expressions of visiting politicians.

en:
As communities grew and your influence continued to expand, Zantanak seemed to have trouble adapting, and one day asked you where he fit into your plans.

Since his only obligation to you was to serve as your bodyguard and advisor, during your discussion with him, you determined that he would in fact have time to pursue other interests, and almost immediately, he asked you if he would be allowed to take a wife.

You granted him permission to wed any woman who would have him, and he seemed satisfied.

Zantanak has not yet chosen a wife, but seems to appreciate the consideration, and as time passes, he seems to settle more and more. He makes friends, saying he is "establishing contacts" and tours the stronghold to "maintain visibility" but it is clear that he is beginning to enjoy his time spent amid mortals.

en:
With the death of the Leviathan, the seas and skies surrounding the island went eerily calm, as though mourning the loss of their master.

A few weeks of searching eventually turned up a ship in the Miser's Purse that could be made seaworthy with a little work, so you relocated your stronghold one last time and made it your project.

When the work was complete, your band piled on and nervously set out into the calm sea, and before long, the island of Lukatt was a distant speck on the horizon as you sailed for the Orc Nation of Tsarath.

en:
After leading such a large band of people, returning to a regular civilian life seemed dull, so instead you traveled to a small community on the frontiers of Tsarath, where bands of nomads roamed and survival was hard-fought.

There, you built a modest homestead for yourself, and you lived out your days working for a satisfying life that felt well-earned.

en:
Your experiences on Lukatt made a return to normal civilian life all but impossible, so you ended up joining a mercenary band in order to prevent yourself from becoming too comfortable.

Though you still managed to keep a small home near a frontier town, you traveled often, and that life suited you better than putting down roots ever had. Your work afforded you an endless variety of interesting new experiences, and life was never boring.
